title: Amazon launches Alexa+ in India with Hindi support
content:
Amazon today announced that its Alexa+ conversational assistant is available in India with Hindi support. The new assistant can hold conversations for longer and maintain context while doing so.
The feature is available to all customers in the country in Early Access in Hindi and English. After the early testing period, the company will make the assistant free for Prime customers. For non-Prime customers, the price would be ₹2,000 per month ($20.85).
The company said that the new Alexa has a more expressive voice and can handle complex multi-step tasks, including ordering groceries from Amazon’s quick commerce service Amazon Now and turning on/off smart home devices. Users can switch between English and Hindi mid-sentence.
Amazon added that Alexa+ is integrated with India-based services such as food delivery service Swiggy, Zomato’s ticket booking platform District, travel websites like TripAdvisor and MakeMyTrip, and restaurant reservation app EazyDiner. The upgraded assistant is also integrated with music streaming services such as Amazon Music and JioSaavn.
In June, TechCrunch reported that the company had invited users to enroll in a testing program for Alexa+, through which they could have conversations with the assistant in Hindi. After that, the company also started testing an English version of Alexa+.
Amazon launched Alexa in India in English in 2017 and added Hindi support in 2019. The country has more than 600 million Hindi speakers, and Amazon is trying to tap into that market with its smart devices and new features. The company didn’t give absolute numbers, but said that its smart home devices have grown by 20% from last year.
Amazon initially announced gen AI-powered Alexa+ in 2025 and made it available to all U.S.-based users in 2026. This year, the company has also launched its new assistant in markets such as the U.K., Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Italy, and Germany with local language context.

report.summary: Amazon launches Alexa+ in India with Hindi and English support, early access free, later free for Prime and ₹2,000 monthly for others.
report.background: Amazon first launched Alexa in India in English in 2017 and added Hindi in 2019. India has more than 600 million Hindi speakers, making it a critical market for voice AI, but earlier assistants often struggled with natural bilingual conversations and complex tasks. Generative AI has renewed competition among voice assistants, with Google, Apple, and regional players improving local-language understanding. Amazon announced gen AI-powered Alexa+ in 2025 and made it available to all U.S. users in 2026, then expanded to the U.K., Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Italy, and Germany with local language context. In June, Amazon began testing Alexa+ in Hindi in India, followed by English testing, setting the stage for this Early Access launch.
key_points: Alexa+ is available in India in Early Access for all customers in Hindi and English. After testing, it will be free for Prime members, while non-Prime users will pay ₹2,000 per month, about $20.85. This pricing pushes Alexa+ deeper into Amazon's subscription ecosystem.

The upgraded assistant can hold longer conversations with context, uses a more expressive voice, and handles complex multi-step tasks. It can order groceries from Amazon Now, control smart home devices, and let users switch between English and Hindi mid-sentence, improving natural bilingual use.

Amazon has integrated Alexa+ with major India-focused services, including Swiggy, Zomato's District, TripAdvisor, MakeMyTrip, and EazyDiner. It also works with Amazon Music and JioSaavn, making the assistant a hub for food delivery, ticketing, travel bookings, restaurant reservations, and music.

The launch follows Hindi and English testing programs started in June. It builds on Amazon's long India presence: Alexa launched in English in 2017 and gained Hindi support in 2019. Amazon says its smart home devices in India grew 20% year over year, though it did not share absolute numbers.

Globally, Amazon is rolling out Alexa+ with local language context after launching in the U.S. and several other markets. India is a key test for Hindi and bilingual conversation, showing how generative AI assistants are moving from English-first tools to locally adapted platforms.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Alexa+ in India signals that voice assistants are becoming generative, multilingual, and commerce-connected. It raises competition for Google Assistant, Gemini, Apple Siri, and local language AI services. For developers, the integrations with Swiggy, Zomato, MakeMyTrip, and others show demand for localized skills, APIs, and conversational commerce tools. For regular users, Alexa+ could make voice control more useful in Hindi and English, especially for daily tasks like groceries, travel, and smart home control. However, non-Prime users face a significant monthly fee, so adoption may depend on Prime bundling and whether the assistant feels reliably better than free alternatives.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch Amazon Alexa Skills Kit and Amazon Bedrock for building voice and generative AI experiences. For open-source alternatives, explore Home Assistant's voice stack with Whisper for speech recognition, Piper for text-to-speech, and Wyoming for local voice pipelines. Rhasspy, Open Voice OS, and Rasa are useful for custom assistants. For Hindi and Indic languages, AI4Bharat's IndicWhisper and IndicTTS are relevant starting points.
